activities.title: Layer Normalization and RMSNorm: Mathematics and Numerical Stability

source_resources.title: Root Mean Square Layer Normalization
source_resources.author: Biao Zhang, Rico Sennrich (University of Edinburgh)
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Variance, standard deviation, and LayerNorm basics.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Primary paper showing that mean-centering in LayerNorm can be discarded without performance loss, speeding up modern LLMs (LLaMA, Gemma).

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Original LayerNorm formulation with mean-centering; RMSNorm is compared directly against it as an optimization.
Batch-dependent statistics; unsuitable for autoregressive sequence modeling.

source_resources.safe_fallback: RMSNorm formulas and numerical comparisons are derived completely in the lesson.
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 4 RMSNorm (Equation 4) and Section 4.1 Invariance Analysis

source_resources.title: On Layer Normalization in the Transformer Architecture
source_resources.author: Ruibin Xiong, Yunchang Yang, Di He, Kai Zheng, Shuxin Zheng, Chen Xing, Huishuai Zhang, Yanyan Lan, Liwei Wang, Tie-Yan Liu
source_resources.license: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license / Open Access
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation and reference under arXiv open access terms; no paper figures or prose reproduced.
source_resources.prerequisites: LayerNorm and residual connections from Days 46-01 and 46-02; gradients from Days 31-36.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Supports the activity's stability claim: Post-LN has large expected gradients near the output at initialization and needs warm-up; Pre-LN trained without warm-up reached comparable results in the paper's experiments.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Freely hosted on arXiv.org; the proofs in the appendix use mean-field assumptions stated in Section 3.3.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The lesson states the Pre-LN and Post-LN formulas and the warm-up finding in its own words.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Liu et al.: Understanding the Difficulty of Training Transformers (EMNLP 2020)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Argues that Post-LN instability comes from amplified dependence on the residual branch and proposes Admin initialization; deeper than this activity needs, so deferred.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Wang et al.: Learning Deep Transformer Models for Machine Translation (ACL 2019)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Reports that pre-norm Transformers train deeper stacks than post-norm ones, but is empirical and specific to translation; Xiong et al. give the gradient analysis this activity asks learners to explain.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Abstract; Section 3.3 Understanding the Transformer at initialization (Theorem 1, gradients of the last layer); Section 4 Experiments (Pre-LN without warm-up)

source_resources.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
source_resources.author: Alec Radford, Jeffrey Wu, Rewon Child, David Luan, Dario Amodei, Ilya Sutskever
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation of foundation language model research.
source_resources.prerequisites: Autoregressive conditional likelihood, cross-entropy loss, perplexity exponentiation.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Example of a widely used decoder-only LM that places layer normalization before each sub-block.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Conditional log-likelihood equations, length normalization factors, and held-out cross-entropy calculations are fully derived in lesson material.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Kaplan et al. Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Focuses on empirical power-law loss curves; Radford et al. establishes the zero-shot log-likelihood task evaluation protocol.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Hoffmann et al. Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Chinchilla)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Optimal compute scaling; Radford provides the fundamental zero-shot conditional probability formulation.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 2.3 Model (layer normalization moved to the input of each sub-block)

source_resources.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
source_resources.author: Hugo Touvron, Louis Martin, Kevin Stone, Peter Albert, Amjad Almahairi, et al.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Example of a widely used decoder-only LLM that normalizes before each sub-layer, with RMSNorm in place of LayerNorm.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The LLaMA-2 prompt structure, token boundary rules, and comparative analysis are fully worked out in curriculum lessons.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Touvron et al. LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Original foundation model paper without conversational chat tuning details; LLaMA-2 formalizes dialogue formatting.
Adopts similar [INST] formatting; LLaMA-2 provides the foundational ablation on system prompt integration.
